feedback.problem:
Use the definition of Laplace transforms to calculate $F(s)=L{f(t)},$ where $f(t)$ is given by 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t},\, & t\le 1 \\ 1\, & t>1.\end{aligned}
$$

$\,F(s)=L{f(t)}=$ {{field-1}},
valid for {{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t},\, & t\le 1 \\ 1\, & t>1\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{5t}\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }1\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{5t-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{(5-s)t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the improper integral diverges if $s\le 0.$

For $s>0,$ we calculate our Laplace transform as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{(5-s)t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{5-s}{[{e}^{(5-s)t}]}_{0}^{1}+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{(5-s)}-1}{5-s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{(5-s)}-1}{5-s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{(\frac{-{e}^{-st}}{s})|}_{1}^{a} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{(5-s)}-1}{5-s}-\frac{1}{s}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }({e}^{-as}-{e}^{-s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{(5-s)}-1}{5-s}-\frac{1}{s}\cdot (0-{e}^{-s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{(5-s)}-1}{5-s}+\frac{{e}^{-s}}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$
